public_body: Mbta Fiscal And Management Control Board
overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via serial phone communications and polling among a quorum outside a posted meeting; it ordered future compliance and reconstructed minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a properly posted meeting. Chair phoned members one by one, then polled them on a plan for the General Manager.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the matters discussed by the Board were within the Board’s jurisdiction and that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when a quorum engaged in serial communication regarding these matters outside of a properly posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Board argued its discussion was not deliberation: it was a staff policy matter needing no vote, and the Chair did not relay other members' views.
Polling Board members by telephone on their positions outside a posted meeting was part of the alleged deliberation outside a properly posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the process of polling Board members outside of a properly posted meeting, as was done here, constitutes a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board may have claimed an emergency justified posting less than 48 hours ahead; the AG reviewed whether the emergency exception applied.
allegations.key_passage: We make no determination as to whether the circumstances here constituted an “emergency,” but note that even in an emergency a public body must post notice as soon as possible and comply with all other requirements of the Open Meeting Law

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements

Within 30 days of receipt of the letter, create meeting minutes capturing the discussions and decisions made through the serial communications, using any means available, including notes and members' recollections
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Board, within 30 days of receipt of this letter, to create meeting minutes capturing the discussions held and decisions made through the serial communications at issue in this determination.
